title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§130, 'Retour sur la tour de Fermat', p. 708 of the manuscript). Grothendieck abstracts a general situation from the Fermat tower.

Setting:
- A profinite group Γ acts on a connected, locally connected topos X with a geometric point x0. In the example, Γ = Γ_Q × S_3 (which he calls N_{0,3}), X = M_{0,3}/Qbar ≅ P^1 − {0,1,∞} (equivalently M'_{0,4}), and x0 is the tangential base point 01.
- Π = π1(X, x0). 𝓜 = π1(X, Γ; x0) is the 'equivariant' fundamental group, an extension 1 → Π → 𝓜 → Γ → 1.
- M = Π^ab, and 𝓜~ = 𝓜/[Π,Π] is an extension of Γ by M. In the example M ≅ Ẑ^2, with the Galois and S_3 actions coming from the Ẑ(1)'s attached to the punctures.
- X'_0 is the universal abelian cover at x0 (the pro-Fermat curve), an M-torsor over X.

What this page proposes:
1. Study the ways of lifting the action of Γ on X to an action of Γ on X'_0. The lift must be compatible with Γ acting on the structure group M, i.e. semilinear: g(λx) = γ_M(λ) g(x). The cancelled earlier formulation was to extend the deck action of M to an action of a larger group compatible with Γ's action on X.
2. More generally, take any M_X-torsor X' on X (M_X the constant sheaf), for example X'_0 or its twist by an M-torsor E (E being the fibre at x0). Study the analogous lifts of the Γ-action from X to X'.
3. The cancelled final paragraph observes the following. 𝓜 acts on the universal cover X~ compatibly with its action on X, extending the deck action of Π. Since [Π,Π] is characteristic in Π, it is normal in 𝓜, so this descends to a canonical action of 𝓜/[Π,Π] = 𝓜~ (called 𝒢 there) on X'_0 = X~/[Π,Π]. On the next page this is denoted θ0, and the other admissible actions θ are compared to it.

The next page reformulates everything in terms of fibres. X' is given by its fibre E with Π acting through M-translations. A compatible action is then an action of 𝓜 on E factoring through 𝓜~ and acting by affine (semilinear) transformations of the torsor E: g(λx) = γ_M(λ)g(x), checked by g λ g^{-1} = γ_M(λ).

Modern summary: we want Γ-equivariant structures on an M-torsor over a Γ-space, where M carries a Γ-action. The full group of semilinear lifts is an extension of (the stabiliser in) Γ by M, here 𝓜~. Actual Γ-actions correspond to splittings of 1 → M → 𝓜~ → Γ → 1. Two such actions differ by 1-cocycles Γ → M, so classes are governed by H^1(Γ, M). The obstruction to existence is the class of the extension 𝓜~ in H^2(Γ, M).

For the Fermat tower: the Γ_Q-part splits because the tangential base point 01 is rational. The S_3-part does not fix 01, so a nontrivial extension or obstruction can arise. Lifts then differ by Kummer-type classes in H^1(Γ_Q, Ẑ(1)^2). This is the setup for the Galois/S_3 action on the pro-Fermat curve.
errors: No mathematical error. The notation is inconsistent: the letter M is used both for Π^ab and (in 'distingué dans M') for the big group 𝓜. The quotient 𝓜/[Π,Π] is called 𝒢 in the cancelled passage but 𝓜~ in (278).

Gap, not error: the page does not say that an honest Γ-action on X'_0 lifting the given one exists iff 1→M→𝓜~→Γ→1 splits. The next page only treats the semilinear (affine) form of the action, not existence or classification.

ideas.what: Equivariant fundamental group π1(X,Γ;x0) of a topos with group action, as an extension of Γ by π1(X,x0)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group of the quotient stack [X/Γ] / equivariant fundamental exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 exact sequence); stacky formulation folklore (Noohi, Zoonekynd for stacks)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX–X (homotopy exact sequence); La Longue Marche (1981) uses π1 of topoi with group actions

ideas.what: Lifting a Γ-action on X to a semilinear Γ-action on an M-torsor, with M a Γ-module: the lifts form an extension of Γ by M; actual actions are splittings, classified by H^1(Γ,M), obstructed by H^2(Γ,M)
ideas.modern_name: Γ-equivariant (semilinear) torsors / equivariant structures on torsors; nonabelian cohomology of extensions
ideas.where_published: Giraud's nonabelian cohomology framework; not specifically in Grothendieck's published texts in this form

ideas.what: Canonical action θ0 of 𝓜/[Π,Π] on the universal abelian cover X'_0 (pro-Fermat curve), with M = Π^ab, used to study the Γ_Q × S_3 action on the Fermat tower
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the tower of Fermat curves / abelian pro-cover of P^1 − {0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986, Annals: profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications); Anderson (1989, hyperadelic gamma function); Coleman; Deligne (1989)
ideas.where_published: Fermat tower appears only in unpublished Longue Marche continuation notes

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the classification of all compatible lifts of the Γ_Q × S_3 action (including the S_3 symmetries) to the pro-Fermat cover and its twists, as torsor-theoretic data. This is meant as a general framework, with the canonical lift θ0 as reference point. The published literature (Ihara, Anderson, Coleman) treats mainly the Γ_Q-action and its Jacobi-sum/gamma-function description, with S_3 symmetry handled more ad hoc.
missed.quote: étudier les relèvements analogues de l'action de Γ sur X en une action Γ sur X', compatible avec l'action Γ sur X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally. It is a clean equivariant-torsor formulation that could organise the S_3-twisted Fermat tower (dihedral/'extended' Galois actions, GT-type symmetries at abelian level). Mathematically it is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine setup: lifting a group action to a torsor compatibly with an action on the structure group. Its interest is mainly historical, as evidence that Grothendieck worked on the Galois × S_3 action on the Fermat tower independently of Ihara/Anderson. The content itself is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'l'action de 𝔽[?]' on the first lines is a bold Γ written over: 'relever l'action de Γ sur X'_0'. The struck '(via M)' / 'sur X'_0' should read 'relever l'action de Γ sur X en une action sur X'_0'.
'un M_X-torseur' is M with subscript X, i.e. the constant sheaf M_X on X.
'déduit [de] X'_0 par produit[?]' plausibly reads 'déduit de X'_0 par twist à l'aide d'un M-torseur E' (contracted product/twist). The word is unclear.
In the cancelled final paragraph, 'distingué dans M' refers to the big group 𝓜 (script M), and the 'M' in 'M opère sur X~' is also 𝓜. 𝒢 = 𝓜/[Π,Π] (= 𝓜~ of (278)).
'l'action de [-M-] Γ sur X' is consistent with the image (scribbled-out 'M' replaced by Γ); similarly 'compatible avec l'action de Γ sur X' (scribbled 'M' replaced by Γ).
